title: Tripmojo
lede: Tripmojo reads booking confirmations from a connected Gmail inbox and assembles them into one day-by-day trip a group shares, with an agent called Mojo handling the chores around it.

points: Flights, hotels, trains and activities found in email become a shared itinerary without manual entry.
Tagging @Mojo in the group chat with a link or Reel extracts places, starts polls and records what the group settled on.
Before travel day Mojo asks for missing passport details, attempts check-in, stores boarding passes and warns of delays and gate changes with a leave-by time.
It also watches booked hotel prices, tracks shared expenses and works on the web as well as mobile.
Early testers report extraction slips: a duplicated traveller from a name spelling variant and a receipt not linked to its booking.

sections.text: Groups planning a trip together whose bookings are spread across several inboxes and whose plans live in a chat thread.
The listing says the app is free on iOS and Android.
